html:
The Chacato, or Chatot, were a Native American people of the upper Apalachicola and Chipola rivers, in what is now the Florida panhandle and nearby Alabama.

Spanish friars built two missions in Chacato villages in 1674 as part of the mission chain of Spanish Florida. The next year many Chacato rebelled against the friars' strict rules and fled, some to the Chiscas and others to their neighbours. Those who stayed lived near the Apalachee missions.

Around 1706 raids by Creek allies of English Carolina drove the survivors west to the French at Mobile in Louisiana. When France gave up the area in 1763 they moved on to Louisiana, and they then fade from the record.
sum: The Chacato, or Chatot, were a Native American people of the upper Apalachicola and Chipola rivers, in what is now the Florida panhandle and nearby Alabama.
